synopsis: The corpus treats FEM alongside DEM and SPH terrain models coupled with a multibody machine: these methods predict granular flow, rutting and localized soil failure with high fidelity, but are very slow [f6468, f6469]. They require very high effort and high-performance computing, are described as unusable for scenario sweeps, and have research-only off-road validation status [f6471, f6474, f6473]. Both Chapter 8 and the glossary recommend restricting their braking-validation use to selected limit cases, with Chapter 8 specifying berms, deep aggregate and severe track-soil interaction [f6472, f13835]. This narrow role reflects two limitations: uncertain soil inputs can overwhelm model fidelity, and evidence that these methods are required for threshold prediction was not found [f6475, f6470].

relations.note: Both recommend selected braking limit cases; Chapter 8 specifies terrain examples.
Unsuitability for scenario sweeps supports restricting use to selected limit cases.
Soil-input uncertainty supports limiting deployment of high-fidelity terrain models.
No evidence of necessity for threshold prediction supports selective rather than routine use.
Very high effort and computing requirements support reserving models for selected cases.
Very slow execution explains why these models are unusable for scenario sweeps.
Localized soil-failure and granular-flow capabilities fit the recommended difficult terrain cases.
Nominal high fidelity is qualified by uncertainty in soil inputs.
